Page.Course.SimpleTitle: In plain words: a study companion with experiments
Page.Course.Simple: This part of the program is a separate teaching unit. It follows the three last modules of a computational neuroscience course: how neurons connect into networks (6), how connections learn from experience (7), and how a brain learns from examples and rewards – and how it can be linked to machines (8). Every lesson has a short explanation on the left and a small laboratory on the right where you can try the idea yourself. At the bottom of each lesson a few questions check whether you got the point.
Page.Course.Guide:
Pick a module card below, or click a lesson title to jump straight into it.
Each lesson: read the theory on the left, then play with the lab on the right.
The yellow “In plain words” box and the “Guide” panel adapt to the current lesson.
Finish with the self-check questions – click a question to reveal the answer.
Page.M6.Title: 6 · Synapses & networks
Page.M6.Subtitle: From a single synapse to feedforward filters and recurrent networks with memory and oscillations
Page.M6.Tip: Module 6: modeling connections, network models and recurrent networks.
Page.M7.Title: 7 · Plasticity & unsupervised learning
Page.M7.Subtitle: Hebbian learning, PCA, clustering, generative models, sparse and predictive coding
Page.M7.Tip: Module 7: synaptic plasticity, unsupervised learning, sparse coding and predictive coding.
Page.M8.Title: 8 · Supervised, reinforcement learning & BCI
Page.M8.Subtitle: Perceptrons and backpropagation, reward prediction with TD learning, actor–critic, bidirectional brain–computer interfaces
Page.M8.Tip: Module 8: neurons as classifiers, reinforcement learning and bidirectional BCIs.

Course.Hub.Title: Computational Neuroscience
Course.Hub.Text: From synapses to networks, from learning rules to rewards and brain–machine interfaces. Fourteen lessons, each with a compact theory sheet, live simulations you can steer, and self-check questions – in English and Hungarian.
Course.Hub.Source: Built from the Hungarian study notes of modules 6–8 of the Computational Neuroscience course (original lecturer: Rajesh Rao). The simulations follow the models of the lectures and of Dayan & Abbott: Theoretical Neuroscience.
Course.Hub.Path.Text: synapse → network → feedback & memory → learning rules → statistics of the world → sparse & predictive codes → classification → reward → closed loop with a machine
Course.Hub.Tip1.Title: How to use a lesson
Course.Hub.Tip1.Text: Read the lead and the concept blocks first. Then try the examples in the lab – each one demonstrates one sentence of the theory. Hover over any ⓘ symbol or slider for an explanation.
Course.Hub.Tip2.Title: For the exam
Course.Hub.Tip2.Text: The “Remember” card lists what you must know; the “Check yourself” questions are taken from the course notes. Try to answer before revealing – then reproduce the effect in the lab.
Course.Hub.Tip3.Title: Connections to the lab
Course.Hub.Tip3.Text: The simulator pages above use the same ideas at full scale: STDP (lesson 7.1 and 8.4), recurrent spiking networks (module 6), and population coding (lessons 6.4 and 6.5).
